annotations.title: A line's stops, how often it runs, and its timetable as a PDF

description:
Describe one public-transport line in Switzerland — a train (S24, IC5, RE33), a tram or bus line (tram 11, bus 31), a boat or a mountain railway — by its directions and the stops of each with the minutes to them, how many trips it makes on a working day, a Saturday and a Sunday with the first, the last and how often it runs, and its page and whole timetable as a PDF to print or save.

Use it for "where does the S24 go", "how often does tram 11 in Zürich run on Sundays", "when is the first and last IC5", "give me the timetable of the S6 as a PDF". For a station's lines and works, station_info; for a journey, plan_journey.

Inputs: line is the line's label as on the vehicle or the board ("S24", "IC 5", "11", "Bus 31"). near narrows a label used in several places: a station or town it calls at, A station or stop name ("Zürich HB", "Bern", "Lausanne, Flon"), an address ("Bahnhofplatz 1, Winterthur"), a named place ("ETH Zürich", "Kunsthaus Zürich"), a town's name in English, French or Italian ("Geneva", "Lucerne"), a coordinate as "geo:47.3769,8.5417", or a place_id returned by find_place ("stop:8503000"). Names are read the way a rider types them; an ambiguous name returns candidates instead of a guess. Without near, the busiest line of that label is described and the others are listed with their towns.

The days are read from the published timetable for the four weeks from today, each kind of day from an ordinary one of them; times are planned.

Example: {"line": "S24", "near": "Zug"}

line.description: The line's label, as on the vehicle or the board: "S24", "IC5", "11".

near.description: A station or town the line calls at, for a label used in several places.
